rules.source: CREC Exclusive Right-to-Buy Listing Contract (BDB24-6-24) §7 compensation blanks; Burnett v. NAR settlement practice changes (eff. 2024-08-17); C.R.S. 12-10-203

payload.summary: Pre-filled buyer-broker fee percentage presented as if standard.

finding.default_analysis: The compensation blank arrives pre-filled with a percentage. Buyer-broker compensation is negotiable and is not set by law or by any MLS rule; the blank could equally hold a flat fee, an hourly rate, or a lower percentage with a cap. Ask what the number would be if you proposed it.

rules.source: CREC BDB24-6-24 §2 brokerage services area blank; CO Division of Real Estate buyer-agency guidance

payload.summary: Agreement scope covers an entire region rather than the search actually underway.

finding.default_analysis: The services-area blank is filled region-wide, obligating the buyer to this broker for ANY purchase anywhere in the territory during the term. The blank could have named one county, one town, or one listing. Region-wide scope plus a backstop clause is how a buyer ends up owing a fee on a property the broker never touched.

payload.summary: Buyer personally backstops the fee if seller-side payment falls through.

all_of: (?:seller|landlord|listing broker(?:age)?)[^.]{0,160}?(?:does not pay|fails? to pay|shall not pay|will not pay)

finding.default_analysis: If the seller or listing brokerage does not pay, the buyer pays the entire unpaid fee at closing — on top of down payment and closing costs. The blank could have capped buyer liability, made the fee contingent on seller-side payment, or struck the backstop entirely. Exposure shown is the pre-filled percentage applied to the configured target price.

rules.source: CREC BDB24-6-24 fee-earned and survival-of-obligations provisions

payload.summary: Fee is earned and survives even when the deal dies on buyer default.

finding.default_analysis: If the buyer defaults on a purchase contract, the broker's fee is still earned, due, and payable — the buyer pays for a closing that never happened, on top of any earnest money already lost. The blank could have limited the fee to transactions that actually close.

rules.source: CREC Contract to Buy and Sell Real Estate, Residential (CBS1-6-24) §3.1 deadline table; §10.2 Inspection Objection

payload.summary: Inspection Objection Deadline — the buyer's cleanest exit ramp.
payload.lever: The Inspection Objection Deadline is a fill-in blank, negotiable line-by-line like every §3.1 date. Sellers read a short window as a strong offer; the buyer's counter is a window just long enough for the inspections that match this property (sewer scope, roof, well/septic where applicable).
payload.risk_if_waived: Waiving or missing it forfeits the unconditional right to object or terminate on physical-condition grounds — adverse discoveries after the deadline generally mean proceeding as-is or defaulting with earnest money at risk.

finding.default_analysis: Negotiable lever: The Inspection Objection Deadline is a fill-in blank, negotiable line-by-line like every §3.1 date — counter with a window just long enough for the inspections this property actually needs. Risk if waived/missed: forfeits the unconditional right to object or terminate on condition grounds; adverse discoveries after the deadline mean proceeding as-is or defaulting with earnest money at risk.

rules.source: CREC CBS1-6-24 §3.1 deadline table; §10.3 Inspection Resolution

payload.summary: Inspection Resolution Deadline — where repair negotiations actually die.
payload.lever: The gap between Objection and Resolution is the real negotiating window for repairs, credits, or price reductions. Width is negotiable; a too-narrow gap pressures the buyer to fold on legitimate objections.
payload.risk_if_waived: If the Resolution Deadline passes without a signed agreement, the buyer's objection is deemed withdrawn under §10.3 and the contract proceeds as-is — silence converts an objection into acceptance.

finding.default_analysis: Negotiable lever: the Objection-to-Resolution gap is the real window for negotiating repairs, credits, or price cuts — keep it wide enough to actually negotiate. Risk if waived/missed: an objection with no signed resolution by this deadline is deemed withdrawn (§10.3) and the contract proceeds as-is; silence converts an objection into acceptance.

rules.source: CREC CBS1-6-24 §3.1 deadline table; §6.2 Appraisal Deadline

payload.summary: Appraisal Deadline — the valuation-gap escape hatch.
payload.lever: Deadline timing relative to the loan deadlines is negotiable, and so is what happens on a low appraisal: objection, renegotiation, or a capped appraisal-gap commitment sized by the BuyerPack max_appraisal_gap_usd, not by the listing agent's ask.
payload.risk_if_waived: Waiving appraisal protection commits the buyer to covering any gap between contract price and appraised value in cash; on a thin-comp property that number is open-ended.

finding.default_analysis: Negotiable lever: appraisal-deadline timing and the low-appraisal remedy are both blanks — objection, renegotiation, or a CAPPED gap commitment sized by your own ceiling, not the listing side's ask. Risk if waived/missed: waiving appraisal protection commits the buyer to paying any contract-vs-appraisal gap in cash, an open-ended number on thin-comp properties.

rules.source: CREC CBS1-6-24 §3.1 deadline table; §5.2 New Loan Availability / Termination

payload.summary: New Loan Availability Deadline — the last clean financing exit.
payload.lever: Position this deadline late enough for underwriting reality (rate locks, appraisal turn-times in Larimer County) — it is the last date the buyer can terminate on financing grounds and keep earnest money.
payload.risk_if_waived: After this deadline a financing failure is a buyer default: earnest money is forfeit and, under fee-survival clauses, broker fees may still be owed on a purchase that never closed.

all_of: (?:new loan availability|loan availability|new loan termination) deadline

finding.default_analysis: Negotiable lever: set this date late enough for underwriting reality — it is the last date to terminate on financing grounds and keep earnest money. Risk if waived/missed: a later financing failure is buyer default — earnest money forfeit, and under fee-survival clauses broker fees may still be owed on a purchase that never closed.

rules.source: C.R.S. Title 32 Article 1 (special districts); DOLA special district transparency portal; Larimer County Assessor tax entity rolls

payload.summary: Metro-district debt service can add 40-70+ mills to the effective tax rate without appearing in the list price.
payload.analysis: Metro-district mill levies are a recurring cost the listing never headlines. Pull the property's total mill levy and the district's debt profile from the transparency portal before pricing an offer; a 60-mill district on a $700k home is roughly $2,900/yr above a comparable non-district home.

detection.note: Detection spec as data per §12 P1-C; the assessor adapter is NOT built in Phase 1.

rules.source: EPA Map of Radon Zones (Larimer County = Zone 1, highest potential); CDPHE radon program; C.R.S. 38-35.7-109 (radon disclosure, eff. 2023-08-07)

payload.summary: Larimer County is EPA radon Zone 1: testing is the norm, not an exotic ask.
payload.analysis: Radon testing during inspection is standard practice in Larimer County and sellers must disclose known radon history (C.R.S. 38-35.7-109). A failed test is a negotiation item: active mitigation typically runs $1,500-$2,500 — ask for it as a credit or repair, never absorb it silently.

rules.source: Colorado State Forest Service Wildfire Risk Assessment (coloradoforestatlas.org); HB23-1288 Fair Access to Insurance (FAIR plan)

payload.summary: Wildfire-exposed foothills properties can be uninsurable or carry premiums that break the monthly budget.
payload.analysis: For any property at moderate-or-higher wildfire risk, obtain an actual insurance quote BEFORE the inspection window closes — non-renewal patterns in the foothills mean the FAIR plan (last-resort coverage, higher cost, lower limits) may be the only option, and lenders require proof of insurability to close.

detection.note: Detection spec as data per §12 P1-C; the risk-layer adapter is NOT built in Phase 1.

rules.source: ECMC (formerly COGCC) Rule 604 location standards (2,000 ft setback framework, eff. 2021-01-15); ECMC well database (ecmc.state.co.us)

payload.summary: Active or permitted oil/gas locations near the parcel affect health, financing, insurance, and resale.
payload.analysis: Query the ECMC well database for active, permitted, or abandoned wells within the setback-relevant radius of the parcel. New-development setbacks are 2,000 ft (Rule 604), but existing wells can sit far closer to existing homes; verify plugging status for abandoned wells and disclose findings to the inspector.

detection.note: Detection spec as data per §12 P1-C; the ECMC adapter is NOT built in Phase 1.
